alabama.variance_standard_note: A variance is granted only where special conditions make literal enforcement of the ordinance an 'unnecessary hardship' and the spirit of the ordinance is still observed. Alabama courts grant variances sparingly, only in peculiar and exceptional circumstances.
alabama.variance_process: Apply to your city or town's board of adjustment (five members) for a variance from the zoning ordinance. The board holds a hearing and can grant the variance only if you show special conditions unique to your property that make strict enforcement an unnecessary hardship, and that the variance will not harm the public interest. You cannot get a variance to allow a use the ordinance forbids.
alabama.appeal_route: An aggrieved party may appeal a board of adjustment decision to the circuit court under Ala. Code § 11-52-81.
alabama.nonconforming_note: A lawful use that predates a zoning change may continue as a grandfathered use until it is lost through abandonment. Expansion and abandonment details are set by local ordinance.
alabama.state_note: Alabama has no single statewide planning agency for homeowners; the Alabama League of Municipalities is the main state-level resource on municipal zoning. County zoning is limited, so most homeowners deal with a city or town board of adjustment.

alaska.variance_standard_note: The statute frames the test as whether literal enforcement would deprive the owner of rights commonly enjoyed by other properties in the district. A variance is barred if the hardship is self-caused, if it would permit a prohibited use, or if it is sought only to relieve money hardship. The wording is unusual and does not track the classic 'unnecessary hardship' formula, so it is flagged as ambiguous below.
alaska.variance_process: Apply to your borough or city planning commission or board of adjustment (or hearing officer), which holds a hearing on the variance. You must show special conditions affecting your property, that the hardship is not of your own making, and that the variance would not allow a prohibited use or simply save you money. Home-rule boroughs are not bound by the state statute and set their own procedures.
alaska.appeal_route: An aggrieved person appeals a variance decision to the superior court under AS 29.40.060, heard solely on the record as an administrative appeal. Alaska Appellate Rule 602(a)(2) generally requires filing the notice of appeal within 30 days after the decision is mailed or distributed, once the decision states it is final.
alaska.nonconforming_note: No state statute protects nonconforming uses; whether a grandfathered use may continue, expand, or is lost by abandonment is set entirely by local ordinance (for example, Anchorage Municipal Code chapter 21.13).
alaska.statute_name: Planning, Platting, and Land Use Regulation
alaska.agency_name: Alaska Department of Commerce, Community & Economic Development, Division of Community and Regional Affairs
alaska.state_note: Much of Alaska has no zoning at all, and home-rule boroughs are exempt from the state framework law, so a homeowner's first step is to find out whether their borough or city even has zoning. The state agency's Local Government Online pages are the starting point for that question.

arizona.variance_standard_note: A variance is granted only if special circumstances (size, shape, topography, location, or surroundings) mean strict enforcement deprives the property of privileges enjoyed by other property in the same district. The hardship must not be self-imposed, and a variance can never allow a prohibited use.
arizona.variance_process: Apply to your city or town board of adjustment (or, in unincorporated areas, the county board of adjustment) for a variance, with a public hearing. You must show the special circumstances of your lot, that the problem is not of your own making, and that the variance keeps with the spirit of the ordinance. The board may attach conditions to protect neighbors.
arizona.appeal_route: A board of adjustment decision is appealed to the superior court. In counties the appeal is heard de novo (a fresh hearing) under A.R.S. § 11-816(D).
arizona.nonconforming_note: A lawful use that predates a zoning change may continue as a grandfathered use. There is no statewide nonconforming-use statute; local ordinances govern, and most end the use after 12 months of continuous nonuse. In counties, A.R.S. § 11-830 allows a nonconforming business use to expand up to 100% with a use permit.
arizona.statute_cite: A.R.S. § 9-462 et seq. (municipal); A.R.S. § 11-801 et seq. (county)
arizona.agency_name: League of Arizona Cities and Towns
arizona.state_note: Community Legal Services serves Maricopa, Yuma, Mohave, Yavapai, and La Paz counties; other counties are served by different legal-aid programs, so check AZLawHelp for your county. Arizona also has strong state limits on local zoning of housing, including accessory dwelling units.

arkansas.variance_standard_note: A variance is granted only where strict enforcement would cause 'undue hardship due to circumstances unique to the individual property' and the variance keeps with the spirit and intent of the ordinance. The board may never grant a variance to allow a use the ordinance forbids in that zone.
arkansas.variance_process: Apply to your city's board of zoning adjustment (at least three members, or the planning commission sitting as the board), which holds a public hearing. You must submit a written explanation of the hardship, show it comes from circumstances unique to your property and not created by you, and show the variance fits the ordinance's purpose. The board may impose conditions to protect adjacent property.
arkansas.appeal_route: Board decisions are appealed to a circuit court of competent jurisdiction under Ark. Code § 14-56-416. The city governing body may by ordinance choose to hear appeals first before they go to court.
arkansas.nonconforming_note: No state statute protects nonconforming uses; the rules are local. Many Arkansas cities end a grandfathered use after a period of discontinuance (for example, six months in Little Rock), so check your city ordinance.
arkansas.state_note: Arkansas law is unusually clear that a variance can never authorize a forbidden use — a homeowner who wants a different use needs a rezoning, not a variance. Legal Aid of Arkansas becomes the sole statewide legal-aid provider in 2026.

california.variance_standard_note: A variance is granted only when special circumstances of the property (size, shape, topography, location, or surroundings) mean strict enforcement deprives it of privileges enjoyed by other property in the same zone. Use variances are prohibited, and financial or personal hardship alone is not grounds.
california.variance_process: Apply to your city or county zoning administrator or board of zoning adjustment for a variance, with a public hearing. You must show the special circumstances of your lot and that the variance will not grant you a special privilege. A denial can usually be appealed first to the planning commission and then to the city council or board of supervisors.
california.appeal_route: After local appeals are exhausted, a variance decision is challenged in superior court by administrative mandamus under Code of Civil Procedure § 1094.5. Government Code § 65009(c)(1)(E) requires the action to be filed and served within 90 days of the decision.
california.nonconforming_note: A lawful pre-existing use may generally continue, but it cannot expand or intensify, and California courts allow cities to phase a nonconforming use out over a reasonable period (amortization). Abandonment and discontinuance rules are local.
california.agency_name: Governor's Office of Land Use and Climate Innovation (LCI, formerly OPR)
california.state_note: State housing laws sharply limit local power to deny housing, including the Housing Accountability Act (Gov. Code § 65589.5) and state accessory-dwelling-unit rules — a homeowner blocked on a housing project may have state-law rights beyond the local variance process.

colorado.variance_standard_note: The municipal statute joins both tests — 'practical difficulties or unnecessary hardships' — and the county statute does the same, so there is no single statewide standard. Local ordinances and boards apply the test differently, and a city may by ordinance take away the board's power to grant use variances entirely.
colorado.variance_process: Apply to your city or county board of adjustment (five members in cities), which holds a hearing. You must show that practical difficulty or unnecessary hardship comes from the shape, size, topography, or other exceptional condition of your property, that the hardship is not self-imposed, and that the variance will not harm the public good. Check whether your city even allows use variances, since many do not.
colorado.appeal_route: A board of adjustment decision is reviewed by the district court by certiorari under C.R.S. § 31-23-307(1), filed not later than 30 days after the board's final action.
colorado.nonconforming_note: No state statute protects nonconforming uses; the rules are local. Typically a grandfathered use may continue on the same land and floor area without enlargement, and it ends by abandonment or violation of the ordinance.
colorado.statute_name: Planning and Zoning (Municipal Zoning Enabling Act)
colorado.statute_cite: Colo. Rev. Stat. § 31-23-201 et seq. (municipal); § 30-28-101 et seq. (county)
colorado.agency_name: Colorado Department of Local Affairs, Division of Local Government
colorado.state_note: Colorado's 2024 land-use laws require local governments to add strategic-growth and water-supply elements to their comprehensive plans by December 31, 2026, so local zoning rules are in flux in many communities.

connecticut.variance_standard_note: Connecticut applies a strict hardship test: a variance requires 'exceptional difficulty or unusual hardship' from conditions especially affecting the parcel. Financial hardship alone is not enough, and a variance needs four concurring board votes with reasons stated on the record.
connecticut.variance_process: Apply to your town's zoning board of appeals, which holds a public hearing. You must prove the hardship comes from the land itself (such as an odd shape or topography), that you cannot make reasonable use of the property under the ordinance, and that the hardship was not created by you. The board must state its reasons on the record.
connecticut.appeal_route: An aggrieved person appeals a board decision to the Superior Court under Conn. Gen. Stat. § 8-8, by service of process within 15 days from the date notice of the decision was published.
connecticut.nonconforming_note: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 8-2 bars zoning regulations from prohibiting the continuance of a nonconforming use existing when the regulations were adopted, and from ending a use solely for nonuse over a set period without regard to the owner's intent. Abandonment requires voluntary discontinuance with intent not to reestablish the use.
connecticut.state_note: A 2025 compromise zoning-reform law (missing-middle housing, parking minimums) takes effect January 1, 2026, which may change what a homeowner can build without a variance. Connecticut's 15-day court appeal deadline is unusually short — act immediately after a denial.

delaware.variance_standard_note: The statute joins both phrases — 'unnecessary hardship or exceptional practical difficulties' — and case law splits them: use variances require unnecessary hardship, while area (dimensional) variances use the looser exceptional-practical-difficulty test. A town may also let a designated official administratively grant a dimensional variance of up to one foot.
delaware.variance_process: Apply to your city or town board of adjustment, which holds a public hearing. For an area variance (setbacks, height, lot size) show exceptional practical difficulty from special conditions of your property; for a use variance show unnecessary hardship and, in New Castle County, get County Council approval by resolution. The board must find the variance will not harm the public good or impair the ordinance's purpose.
delaware.appeal_route: An aggrieved person petitions the Superior Court for a writ of certiorari under 22 Del. C. § 328, within 30 days after the decision is filed in the office of the board.
delaware.nonconforming_note: No statewide nonconforming-use rule was found; whether a grandfathered use exists is a question of fact decided by the board of adjustment after public notice and hearing under the local ordinance.
delaware.statute_cite: 22 Del. C. § 301 et seq. (municipal); 9 Del. C. § 1313 (New Castle County); 9 Del. C. § 6917 (Kent and Sussex Counties)
delaware.agency_name: Delaware Office of State Planning Coordination
delaware.state_note: Delaware's PLUS (Preliminary Land Use Service) pre-application review process gives homeowners and developers early state-agency feedback on land-use proposals before they reach the local board.

florida.variance_standard_note: Florida has no statewide variance standard; each city and county sets its own test in its land development regulations. The common formulation is unnecessary hardship where special conditions peculiar to the land deprive the owner of rights commonly enjoyed by others in the district, while some cities also offer a looser practical-difficulty variance.
florida.variance_process: Apply to your city or county board of adjustment (or other designated local board) for a variance, with a public hearing. You must meet your local ordinance's test — usually showing special conditions unique to your lot, that the hardship is not self-created, and that the variance will not harm neighbors or the public interest. Check your local code first, because the test and the deciding body vary by jurisdiction.
florida.appeal_route: Quasi-judicial land-use decisions, including variance denials, are reviewed by petition for writ of certiorari to the circuit court under Florida Rule of Appellate Procedure 9.100(c), filed within 30 days of rendition of the decision.
florida.nonconforming_note: No statewide nonconforming-use statute was identified; grandfathered uses are governed by local ordinance. Typically a lawful pre-existing use may continue but not expand, and it is lost by abandonment or discontinuance for the period your local code sets.
florida.state_note: The Bert Harris Private Property Rights Protection Act (Fla. Stat. § 70.001) lets owners seek relief when government action inordinately burdens their property, and the Live Local Act preempts local use, height, and density limits for qualifying affordable-housing developments.

georgia.variance_standard_note: The state Zoning Procedures Law sets procedures, not the substantive test, so the variance standard is set by each city and county. Most local ordinances require a finding of unnecessary hardship or 'extraordinary and exceptional conditions' (such as size, shape, or topography) where literal enforcement deprives the property of privileges enjoyed by others.
georgia.variance_process: Apply to your city or county board of zoning appeals (or other local body designated by ordinance), which holds a quasi-judicial public hearing with at least 30 days' notice. You must show the hardship comes from extraordinary conditions of your property, not from your own actions, and present evidence at the hearing, since the decision is made on the record. The local government must have adopted written standards for quasi-judicial decisions.
georgia.appeal_route: Quasi-judicial decisions, including variance denials, are reviewed by the superior court by petition for review under Title 5, on the record, per O.C.G.A. § 36-66-5.1(a)(2).
georgia.nonconforming_note: No statewide nonconforming-use statute was identified; the rules are local. Typically a lawful pre-existing use may continue but not expand or intensify, and discontinuance — commonly 12 months — is treated as abandonment, though Georgia case law has historically looked for intent to abandon.
georgia.state_note: Georgia Legal Services Program serves 154 counties outside metro Atlanta; metro Atlanta is served by Atlanta Legal Aid Society. Georgia's 2022 reforms replaced the old writ-of-certiorari appeal with a uniform petition-for-review process in superior court.

hawaii.variance_standard_note: Hawaii has no single statewide variance test. HRS § 46-4 delegates zoning to the four counties, so each county sets its own standard — typically some form of special or unusual circumstances plus no reasonable alternative use.
hawaii.variance_process: Apply to your county planning department or board of variance and appeals (each county names it differently). You show the special circumstances of your lot, that no reasonable alternative exists, and that the variance fits the general plan and will not harm neighbors. The board holds a public hearing and decides.
hawaii.appeal_route: A final county board decision is appealed to the Circuit Court for judicial review on the record under HRS § 91-14, within 30 days after service of the final decision. The court reviews the record rather than holding a new trial.
hawaii.nonconforming_note: HRS § 46-4(a) says neither the statute nor any county ordinance may prohibit the continued lawful use of a building or premises for the purpose it was used for when the zoning took effect. Counties have debated phasing out (amortizing) some uses, especially short-term rentals, so check your county's current rules.
hawaii.statute_name: County Zoning and State Land Use Law
hawaii.agency_name: Hawaii Office of Planning and Sustainable Development, Land Use Division
hawaii.state_note: Hawaii is unique: the state itself sorts all land into four districts (urban, rural, agricultural, conservation) under HRS Chapter 205, and the Land Use Commission decides district boundary changes. A homeowner may need a state district change or special permit before county zoning even applies.

idaho.variance_standard_note: Idaho Code § 67-6516 allows a variance only on a showing of undue hardship because of characteristics of the site, and only if it is not in conflict with the public interest. It is not a right or a special privilege.
idaho.variance_process: Apply to your city or county planning and zoning commission (or board of adjustment, depending on the local ordinance). A variance can only change bulk and placement rules — lot size, setbacks, height, parking — not the allowed use of the land. Adjoining owners must get notice and a chance to be heard before it is granted.
idaho.appeal_route: An affected person aggrieved by a final decision may seek judicial review in district court under the Idaho Administrative Procedure Act, Idaho Code § 67-6521(1)(d). You must first ask the local body for reconsideration within 14 days under Idaho Code § 67-6535(2)(b), which pauses the appeal clock.
idaho.nonconforming_note: The state statute does not set a single statewide rule for how long a grandfathered use lasts. Local ordinances generally let a lawful nonconforming use continue if it is not expanded, and end it on discontinuance or abandonment (commonly one year locally) or if damage exceeds half the assessed value.
idaho.state_note: Idaho variances are dimensional only: you cannot get a variance to use land for a purpose the zone forbids — that needs a conditional use permit or a rezoning instead.

illinois.variance_standard_note: The statute couples both phrases — variations are allowed only where there are 'practical difficulties or particular hardship' — and the detailed findings differ between Chicago (65 ILCS 5/11-13-4) and smaller municipalities (65 ILCS 5/11-13-5). In practice local boards apply a hardship-style test.
illinois.variance_process: Apply to your local zoning board of appeals, which holds a public hearing and makes findings. You must show your property cannot yield a reasonable return if used only as allowed, that your plight comes from unique circumstances of the property, and that the variation will not alter the essential character of the neighborhood.
illinois.appeal_route: Board of appeals decisions are reviewable in circuit court under the Administrative Review Law, 735 ILCS 5/3-101 et seq., per 65 ILCS 5/11-13-13. The complaint and summons must be filed within 35 days after a copy of the decision was served on the affected party.
illinois.nonconforming_note: There is no single statewide abandonment period; local ordinances govern. The general pattern is that a lawful nonconforming use may continue while otherwise lawful, may not be expanded or intensified, and ends when it is discontinued for the period your local ordinance sets (for example, 18 continuous months in Chicago for most uses).
illinois.state_note: Illinois has no single statewide legal aid firm: Prairie State serves 36 northern and central Illinois counties, while Land of Lincoln Legal Aid serves central and southern Illinois. Check which one covers your county before applying.

indiana.variance_standard_note: Indiana splits the test by statute: a variance of use requires unnecessary hardship (IC 36-7-4-918.4), while a variance from development standards such as height, bulk, or area requires only practical difficulties (IC 36-7-4-918.5). A local ordinance may set a stricter standard than practical difficulty for development standards.
indiana.variance_process: Apply to your local board of zoning appeals, which holds a public hearing. For a use variance you must show the variance will not harm public health, safety, or welfare, will not substantially hurt neighboring property values, arises from a condition peculiar to your property, and that strict application would be an unnecessary hardship. Development-standard variances need only the first three findings plus practical difficulties.
indiana.appeal_route: Review is by certiorari: an aggrieved person files a verified petition in the circuit or superior court of the county where the property is located, under IC 36-7-4-1003. Note that Indiana courts have recently disputed whether the 30 days runs from the board's vote or from its written findings, so file promptly and get legal advice on the trigger date.
indiana.nonconforming_note: The statute protects some nonconforming uses expressly: an agricultural nonconforming use may not be terminated if maintained for at least any 3-year period in a 5-year period (IC 36-7-4-616), and a damaged or destroyed legal nonconforming home may be rebuilt on the same foundation footprint (IC 36-7-4-1019). Other abandonment periods are set by local ordinance (commonly 6 months to 2 years), and the person claiming a nonconforming use bears the burden of proof.
indiana.agency_name: Indiana Office of Community and Rural Affairs
indiana.state_note: Indiana's use-versus-development-standards split is one of the clearest in the country, and it matters: a setback or height request faces a much easier test than asking to run a business in a residential zone.

iowa.variance_standard_note: Iowa splits the test by statute: a use variance requires unnecessary hardship (Iowa Code § 414.12(3)), while a variance from area, dimensional, or other numerical limits requires only practical difficulties (Iowa Code § 414.12(4), added by 2025 Acts ch. 33, effective July 1, 2025).
iowa.variance_process: Apply to your city or county board of adjustment, which holds a public hearing. For a dimensional variance you must prove the difficulties are unique to your property, not self-created, and that granting it will not significantly alter the essential character of the surrounding neighborhood. Use variances face the stricter unnecessary-hardship test and should be granted sparingly.
iowa.appeal_route: Appeal by verified petition for certiorari to the district court under Iowa Code § 414.15. The Iowa Supreme Court has held the 30-day clock is triggered when the board posts the actual decision on its public website (Burroughs v. City of Davenport Zoning Board of Adjustment, 2018).
iowa.nonconforming_note: Iowa Code § 414.1 protects a lawful nonconforming use tied to a preexisting home or home site: a city may not impose new conditions that would prevent it from continuing, except where the owner discontinued or abandoned it for the period set by ordinance, which must be at least one year (unless the discontinuance was caused by circumstances outside the owner's control).
iowa.state_note: Iowa's 2025 change matters for homeowners: setback, lot-size, height, and parking requests now use the easier practical-difficulties test, while asking for a use the zone forbids still needs unnecessary hardship.

kansas.variance_standard_note: K.S.A. 12-759(e)(1) allows a variance only where literal enforcement results in unnecessary hardship due to special conditions, and it expressly says a variance 'shall not permit any use not permitted by the zoning regulations in such district' — so Kansas variances are dimensional only.
kansas.variance_process: Apply to your city or county board of zoning appeals, which holds a public hearing with at least 20 days' published notice. You must show a unique condition not ordinarily found in the same zone and not created by you, that strict application would be an unnecessary hardship, that neighbors' rights and public health and safety will not suffer, and that you are asking for the minimum variance possible.
kansas.appeal_route: Any person dissatisfied with a board of zoning appeals decision may bring an action in the district court of the county to determine its reasonableness, under K.S.A. 12-759(f) and 12-760, filed within 30 days of the final decision.
kansas.nonconforming_note: K.S.A. 12-758(a) says zoning regulations 'shall not apply to the existing use of any building or land,' though they do apply to any change in use. If a nonconforming building is damaged by more than 50 percent of its fair market value, it may not be restored unless its use conforms. Local abandonment periods (commonly 12 months) are set by local ordinance.
kansas.statute_name: Planning, Zoning and Subdivision Regulations in Cities and Counties
kansas.state_note: Kansas law also exempts agricultural land and buildings used for agricultural purposes from city and county zoning (K.S.A. 12-758(b)), except for floodplain regulations.

kentucky.variance_standard_note: Kentucky defines a variance as a departure from dimensional terms only (KRS 100.111(24)), and KRS 100.243 requires findings that strict application would deprive the applicant of reasonable use of the land or create unnecessary hardship, arising from special circumstances not generally applying to nearby land in the same zone.
kentucky.variance_process: Apply to your local board of adjustment, which holds a hearing and may attach reasonable conditions. You must show the variance will not harm public health, safety, or welfare, will not alter the essential character of the area, will not cause a hazard or nuisance, and will not unreasonably get around the zoning rules. The board must deny a variance that arises from willful violations, and a granted variance runs with the land (KRS 100.251).
kentucky.appeal_route: Appeal from a final action of the board of adjustment goes to the Circuit Court of the county where the property lies, under KRS 100.347. As amended effective June 27, 2025, the appellant must also own real property within the same zone as the subject property, and the final action is deemed to occur on the calendar date the vote is taken.
kentucky.nonconforming_note: KRS 100.253(1) says a lawful use of a building or premises existing when zoning regulations were adopted may be continued although it does not conform. The board may not allow it to be enlarged beyond its scope and area at adoption, or changed to a different nonconforming use unless the new use is in the same or a more restrictive classification.
kentucky.legal_aid_name: Kentucky Justice Online (Legal Aid Network of Kentucky)
kentucky.state_note: Kentucky has four regional legal aid programs and no single statewide firm; Kentucky Justice Online is their shared statewide portal and routes you to the program serving your county. Also note KRS 100.253(3): a use that existed illegally but continuously for 10 years with no adverse action by the zoning official is deemed a nonconforming use, except in the largest counties and consolidated governments.

louisiana.variance_standard_note: The statute couples both phrases: the board of adjustment may vary regulations 'where there are practical difficulties or unnecessary hardships in the way of carrying out the strict letter of the ordinance' (R.S. 33:4727). Local ordinances, such as New Orleans, apply detailed findings under that combined standard, so the classification is genuinely ambiguous.
louisiana.variance_process: Apply to your local board of adjustment, which holds a public hearing. You must show peculiar special conditions of your property, not created by you, that literal enforcement deprives you of rights commonly enjoyed by other properties in the same district, and that the hardship is real and not mere inconvenience or a wish for more profit.
louisiana.appeal_route: Any person aggrieved by a board of adjustment decision may present a verified petition to the district court of the parish or city where the property is located, under R.S. 33:4727(E)(1). The court may issue a writ of certiorari to the board to review the decision.
louisiana.nonconforming_note: A lawful use existing when zoning was enacted may be continued, but R.S. 33:140.50.31 lets the local council provide for its termination by specifying a period or a formula allowing a reasonable period to recover the investment (amortization), or with adequate compensation by a court. Nonconforming signs and billboards may also be amortized under R.S. 33:4722, and local ordinances view nonconformities narrowly and limit expansion.
louisiana.state_note: Louisiana has no single statewide legal aid firm: Southeast Louisiana Legal Services covers 22 southeast parishes, while Acadiana Legal Service Corporation serves the rest of the state. Louisiana is also unusual in that parishes (counties) were not granted zoning authority until decades after municipalities.

maine.variance_standard_note: Maine uses a strict undue-hardship test: under 30-A M.R.S. § 4353(4) the board of appeals may grant a variance only if all four findings are met — the land cannot yield a reasonable return without it, the need comes from unique circumstances of the property, it will not alter the essential character of the locality, and the hardship was not caused by the petitioner or a prior owner.
maine.variance_process: Apply to your municipal board of appeals, which holds a hearing. You must prove all four undue-hardship findings, and a municipality may by ordinance add limits, including requiring that the variance be for a use already permitted in that zone. If granted, the variance certificate must be recorded in the registry of deeds within 90 days of final written approval or the variance is void.
maine.appeal_route: A board of appeals decision is appealed to Superior Court under Maine Rule of Civil Procedure 80B, per 30-A M.R.S. § 2691(3)(G). The Maine Supreme Judicial Court has held the clock runs from the date of the vote on the original decision, not from later adoption of written findings (Beckford v. Town of Clifton, 2014 ME 156).
maine.nonconforming_note: Protection is mainly set by local ordinance; the state rule that is spelled out is for shoreland areas, where 38 M.R.S. § 958 lets an existing lawful building, structure, or use continue and be repaired or improved, but a nonconforming use other than single-family residential that is discontinued for one year is deemed abandoned. Local ordinances commonly set discontinuance periods of two years or more.
maine.agency_name: Maine Office of Community Affairs, Municipal Planning Assistance Program
maine.state_note: Maine has separate, narrower variance exceptions worth knowing about: a disability variance, a setback variance for single-family dwellings, and other special cases under 30-A M.R.S. § 4353(4-A), (4-B), and (4-C) and § 4353-A. Maine also has a separate Land Use Planning Commission for the unorganized territories, where there are no towns to zone.

maryland.variance_standard_note: Maryland's statute uses 'unwarranted hardship' and 'exceptional practical difficulty' language (Land Use § 4-203), and courts and counties apply a stricter unnecessary-hardship test to use variances and a looser practical-difficulty test to area variances, so the standard varies by the kind of variance and by county.
maryland.variance_process: Apply to your county or municipal board of appeals, which holds a hearing and decides. You must show the hardship comes from the property itself — for example, exceptional narrowness, shallowness, shape, or topography — that it is not self-created or merely financial, and that the variance is the minimum adjustment needed.
maryland.appeal_route: Any aggrieved person, taxpayer, or officer or unit of the local jurisdiction may file a request for judicial review of a board of appeals decision in the circuit court of the county, under Land Use § 4-401 and Maryland Rules Title 7, Chapter 200. The petition is due within 30 days after the decision is filed in the office of the board.
maryland.nonconforming_note: There is no single statewide abandonment rule; it turns on the local ordinance and on case law. Maryland courts require both an intent to relinquish the use and an overt act or failure to act consistent with that intent, so mere cessation alone does not always end the use — but local ordinances commonly deem a use abandoned after 6 to 12 months of discontinuance, so the local ordinance controls the outcome.
maryland.state_note: Maryland is distinctive because local zoning must be consistent with the local comprehensive plan, and in Montgomery and Prince George's Counties the zoning is administered under a separate regional-district system (Land Use Division II). Rezoning outside a comprehensive rezoning generally requires proof of a substantial change in the neighborhood or a mistake in the last plan.

massachusetts.variance_standard_note: The Zoning Act requires a showing of substantial hardship, financial or otherwise, caused by soil conditions, shape, or topography unique to the lot. A use variance is barred unless the local ordinance expressly permits use variances.
massachusetts.variance_process: Apply or appeal to the local permit granting authority (usually the zoning board of appeals) for a variance from the zoning ordinance or by-law. The board holds a public hearing with published and mailed notice, then must make specific written findings of hardship, no substantial detriment to the public good, and no derogation from the ordinance's intent.
massachusetts.appeal_route: An aggrieved person appeals to the Land Court or the Superior Court (or Housing/District Court where available) under G.L. c. 40A, § 17, asking that the decision be annulled; the court reviews the board's legal conclusions with deference but decides facts largely fresh.
massachusetts.nonconforming_note: Under G.L. c. 40A, § 6, a structure or use lawfully in existence before a zoning change may continue. It may be extended or altered only if the board finds the change will not be substantially more detrimental to the neighborhood, and a local bylaw may end protection after two or more years of non-use.
massachusetts.state_note: Massachusetts is one of the strictest variance states: the hardship must come from the land itself (soil, shape, topography), not personal or financial circumstances alone. Reform bills to replace the hardship test with a practical-difficulty test have been proposed but the substantial-hardship standard in § 10 remains the current law.

michigan.variance_standard_note: Michigan splits the test: a dimensional (nonuse) variance requires practical difficulties, while a use variance requires unnecessary hardship. Use variances also need a two-thirds vote of the zoning board of appeals and are only available in cities and villages, plus townships and counties that authorized them before February 15, 2006.
michigan.variance_process: Apply to the local zoning board of appeals, which holds a hearing and applies the standards set in the local ordinance. Show that the problem comes from unique conditions of the property, not something you created, and that the variance keeps the spirit of the ordinance while doing substantial justice.
michigan.appeal_route: An aggrieved party appeals to the circuit court for the county where the property is located under MCL 125.3606. The court reviews the record to check the decision complies with the constitution and laws, is supported by competent evidence, and was not arbitrary.
michigan.appeal_deadline: 30 days after the board issues its written decision, or 21 days after the board approves the minutes of its decision, whichever comes first
michigan.nonconforming_note: Under MCL 125.3208, a use lawful when a zoning ordinance or amendment was adopted may continue even though it no longer conforms. The local ordinance may set terms for completion, resumption, restoration, reconstruction, extension, or substitution, and the locality may buy out or condemn a nonconforming use.
michigan.state_note: Michigan consolidated its old county, township, and city/village zoning acts into one act in 2006, but use variances remain unusually restricted: many townships and counties simply cannot grant them at all.

minnesota.variance_standard_note: Minnesota uses a three-factor practical-difficulties test under Minn. Stat. § 462.357, subd. 6: the owner proposes a reasonable use not allowed by the ordinance, the plight comes from circumstances unique to the property and not created by the owner, and the variance will not alter the essential character of the locality. Economic considerations alone do not count, and no variance may allow a use prohibited in the district.
minnesota.variance_process: Apply to the local board of adjustment and appeals (often the city council acting as the board), which holds a hearing and must find all three practical-difficulties factors plus harmony with the ordinance's general purposes and consistency with the comprehensive plan. The board may attach conditions to protect neighbors and the public interest.
minnesota.appeal_route: An aggrieved person may seek judicial review in district court under Minn. Stat. § 462.361, after exhausting local remedies. The court reviews the local decision on the record.
minnesota.nonconforming_note: Under Minn. Stat. § 462.357, subd. 1e, a lawful nonconformity may continue, including through repair, replacement, restoration, maintenance, or improvement, but not expansion unless the ordinance allows it. Protection ends if the use is discontinued for more than one year or destroyed by fire or other peril to more than 50 percent of its market value without a building permit application within 180 days; amortization is prohibited by subd. 1c.
minnesota.state_note: Minnesota changed the test in 2011 (2011 Minn. Laws ch. 19): the old 'undue hardship' standard, which required showing the property could not be put to any reasonable use, was replaced with the looser practical-difficulties test after the Minnesota Supreme Court's decision in Krummenacher v. City of Minnetonka (2010). The same test applies in counties under Minn. Stat. § 394.27, subd. 7.

mississippi.variance_standard_note: Mississippi follows the unnecessary-hardship test: the board of adjustment may grant a variance only where strict enforcement would cause unnecessary hardship from extraordinary and exceptional conditions unique to the property. The state enabling act leaves most variance criteria to the local ordinance, so the exact findings required vary by city and county.
mississippi.variance_process: Apply to the local board of adjustment (or the governing body where no separate board exists), which hears the request at a public hearing. Show exceptional conditions peculiar to your property, that the ordinance effectively prohibits or unreasonably restricts its use, and that the variance will not harm neighbors or the character of the district.
mississippi.appeal_route: An aggrieved person appeals a municipal or county governing body's decision to the circuit court by bill of exceptions under Miss. Code Ann. § 11-51-75. The circuit court decides the case on the record made below as an appellate court.
mississippi.nonconforming_note: Mississippi has no statewide statute spelling out nonconforming-use protection; protection comes from the local ordinance and case law, which generally allow a lawfully established use to continue. The exemption can be lost by a change in the use or by abandonment, on terms set by the local ordinance (see Barrett v. Hinds County).
mississippi.state_note: Mississippi's appeal deadline is one of the shortest in the country at 10 days, and it runs from the adjournment of the meeting at which the decision was made, so a homeowner must act almost immediately after a denial.

missouri.variance_standard_note: The statute, Mo. Rev. Stat. § 89.090, lets the board of adjustment grant a variance where there are 'practical difficulties or unnecessary hardship,' without splitting the two tests. In practice local ordinances apply practical difficulty to dimensional (non-use) variances and unnecessary hardship to use variances.
missouri.variance_process: Apply to the local board of adjustment, which holds a hearing and may grant the variance if strict enforcement would cause practical difficulties or unnecessary hardship and the grant keeps the spirit of the ordinance, secures public safety and welfare, and does substantial justice. Four concurring votes of the board are needed to grant a variance.
missouri.appeal_route: An aggrieved person petitions the circuit court of the county or city where the property is located for a writ of certiorari under Mo. Rev. Stat. § 89.110. The court reviews the board's decision for illegality and may take additional evidence on procedural matters.
missouri.nonconforming_note: Missouri's state zoning statutes do not set a general nonconforming-use rule; protection for a lawful pre-existing use comes from the local ordinance and court decisions. Local ordinances typically let the use continue but bar its expansion, and abandonment can end it, so the local ordinance controls.
missouri.statute_name: Zoning and Planning (cities, towns and villages)
missouri.state_note: In a city of 350,000 or more located in more than one county, the board of adjustment has no power at all to vary an ordinance relating to the use of land, so use variances are effectively unavailable there.

montana.variance_standard_note: Montana uses the unnecessary-hardship test: a variance is allowed where, owing to special conditions, literal enforcement would result in unnecessary hardship, the grant is not contrary to the public interest, and the spirit of the ordinance is observed. The 2023 Montana Land Use Planning Act restates the same test, adding that the hardship must not be self-imposed.
montana.variance_process: Apply to the local board of adjustment, which may grant a variance in appropriate cases subject to conditions and safeguards. Show special conditions peculiar to your property, that strict enforcement causes unnecessary hardship, and that the variance will not harm the public interest; four concurring votes are required.
montana.appeal_route: A person aggrieved by a board of adjustment decision may petition the district court (court of record) under Mont. Code Ann. § 76-2-327. The court reviews the decision for illegality.
montana.nonconforming_note: Zoning regulations must allow a lawful nonconforming use to continue (Mont. Code Ann. § 76-2-208 for counties; § 76-25-301(8) under the 2023 act), but the local government may set grounds for ending it based on changes to or abandonment of the use. Any ambiguity about whether a nonconforming use is allowed must be interpreted in favor of the use.
montana.agency_name: Montana League of Cities and Towns
montana.state_note: Montana overhauled its land-use law in 2023 with the Montana Land Use Planning Act (Title 76, Chapter 25), which requires larger local governments to zone in substantial compliance with an adopted land use plan; the older county and municipal zoning framework in Title 76, Chapter 2 still applies alongside it.

nebraska.variance_standard_note: Nebraska's statute blends both phrases, but the board must find undue hardship: strict application would produce undue hardship not shared generally by other properties in the district, the variance will not harm adjacent property or change the district's character, and the hardship is demonstrable and exceptional rather than for convenience, profit, or caprice.
nebraska.variance_process: Apply to the local board of adjustment, which hears the request and may grant a variance only if it makes all four findings in Neb. Rev. Stat. § 19-910(2). The hardship must come from exceptional narrowness, shallowness, shape, topography, or another extraordinary condition of the specific property.
nebraska.appeal_route: An aggrieved person presents a verified petition to the district court under Neb. Rev. Stat. § 19-912, alleging the board's decision is illegal in whole or in part. The court hears and determines the case and may affirm, reverse, or modify the decision.
nebraska.nonconforming_note: Under Neb. Rev. Stat. § 19-904.01, a use existing and lawful when a zoning regulation or amendment was adopted may continue, and may be extended through the same building if no structural alteration is made for that purpose. The right is forfeited if the nonconforming use is discontinued for 12 months, and the local ordinance may provide for termination, including by an amortization schedule.
nebraska.statute_name: Cities and Villages; Laws Applicable to More Than One and Less Than All Classes (zoning)
nebraska.state_note: Nebraska's 15-day appeal deadline is unusually short, and it runs from the filing of the board's decision in the board's office, so a homeowner should get the decision date in writing immediately. Counties have a parallel 15-day appeal rule under Neb. Rev. Stat. § 23-168.04.

nevada.variance_standard_note: Nevada's board-of-adjustment statute, NRS 278.300(1)(c), pairs 'peculiar and exceptional practical difficulties' with 'exceptional and undue hardships' in a single test tied to the property's narrowness, shape, topography, or other extraordinary condition. It does not split use and area variances, and planning commissions and governing bodies may also grant variances under NRS 278.315, so the practical standard depends on which local body decides.
nevada.variance_process: Apply to the local board of adjustment (or the planning commission or hearing examiner where the ordinance gives them that power), which holds a hearing and may grant the variance if strict enforcement would cause peculiar and exceptional practical difficulties or undue hardship and the relief can be granted without substantial detriment to the public good or the ordinance's intent.
nevada.appeal_route: The route depends on the local ordinance: the aggrieved person typically appeals first to the governing body, then files a petition for judicial review in the district court of the proper county under NRS 278.310(3) and 278.3195(4). The district court reviews the decision on the record.
nevada.nonconforming_note: Nevada's state planning and zoning chapter has no general nonconforming-use continuation statute (it addresses only nonconforming outdoor advertising structures in NRS 278.0215). Protection for a lawful pre-existing use comes from the local ordinance, which typically lets it continue until removed or abandoned and bars expansion.
nevada.agency_name: Nevada League of Cities and Municipalities
nevada.state_note: Nevada requires each governing body to adopt an ordinance letting aggrieved persons appeal land-use decisions to the governing body first, and the governing body must decide within 45 days in counties of 700,000 or more and 60 days elsewhere, so a homeowner should expect a two-step appeal before reaching court.

new hampshire.variance_standard_note: New Hampshire applies a five-factor test under RSA 674:33, with unnecessary hardship as the key factor. Hardship means either that no fair and substantial relationship exists between the ordinance's purpose and its application to the property and the proposed use is reasonable, or, failing that, that the property cannot reasonably be used in strict conformance with the ordinance.
new hampshire.variance_process: Apply to the local zoning board of adjustment, usually after a permit denial, and prove all five criteria: not contrary to the public interest, spirit of the ordinance observed, substantial justice done, surrounding property values not diminished, and unnecessary hardship. The board holds a public hearing and decides by a concurring vote of three members.
new hampshire.appeal_route: First file a motion for rehearing with the zoning board of adjustment within 30 days under RSA 677:2; no court appeal is allowed without it. Then petition the superior court under RSA 677:4, which reviews the decision on the certified record and reverses only for legal error or unreasonableness.
new hampshire.nonconforming_note: A lawful use or structure that predates a zoning change may generally continue as a nonconforming use, but expansion, enlargement, and abandonment are controlled by the local ordinance, so the protection is only as broad as the town or city ordinance allows.
new hampshire.statute_name: Local Land Use Planning and Regulatory Powers
new hampshire.state_note: New Hampshire's rehearing requirement is a trap for the unwary: missing the 30-day motion for rehearing ends the appeal entirely, and any ground not raised in that motion generally cannot be argued in court. A granted variance must be exercised within two years or it expires.

new jersey.variance_standard_note: New Jersey has three different variance tracks under N.J.S.A. 40:55D-70: (c)(1) hardship or practical-difficulty variances for bulk and dimensional rules, (c)(2) flexible variances where the benefits substantially outweigh any detriment, and (d) use variances granted only for 'special reasons' where the benefits substantially outweigh the detriment without substantially impairing the zone plan.
new jersey.variance_process: Apply to the municipal zoning board of adjustment, which holds a public hearing and decides the case on proofs. A (c) bulk variance needs a majority vote, while a (d) use variance needs at least five affirmative votes; the board must make findings that the variance can be granted without substantial impairment of the zone plan and zoning ordinance.
new jersey.appeal_route: Challenge a board decision in the Law Division of the Superior Court by an action in lieu of prerogative writs under Court Rule 4:69. The court reviews the record for whether the board acted arbitrarily, capriciously, or unreasonably.
new jersey.nonconforming_note: A lawful use or structure that predates the ordinance may generally continue as a nonconforming use, and may be repaired or restored, but expanding it or changing it to another nonconforming use requires a (d) use variance, and abandonment can end the protection.
new jersey.agency_name: New Jersey State League of Municipalities
new jersey.state_note: The 45-day clock runs from the first publication of the board's decision in the official newspaper, not from the vote, so a homeowner should watch for the published notice. New Jersey also requires a separate 'special reasons' showing for use variances, and inherently beneficial uses such as schools and hospitals get a lighter burden.

new mexico.variance_standard_note: A variance requires unnecessary hardship: literal enforcement of the ordinance, owing to special conditions, would cause unnecessary hardship, and the variance must not be contrary to the public interest and must serve substantial justice. There is no separate looser test for area variances in the state statute.
new mexico.variance_process: Apply to the local zoning authority (the county or municipal governing body, or its board of adjustment where one exists) after a denial by the zoning enforcement officer. The zoning authority holds a hearing and must find the hardship, public-interest, spirit-of-the-ordinance and comprehensive-plan conditions in NMSA 1978, Section 3-21-8.
new mexico.appeal_route: A zoning authority decision is appealed to district court as an administrative appeal, reviewed on the record made below rather than as a new trial.
new mexico.nonconforming_note: The state enabling act does not set a statewide nonconforming-use rule, so protection depends on the local ordinance. In practice a lawful pre-existing use may usually continue, but it generally may not be enlarged or intensified, and it is lost if abandoned or discontinued for the period the local ordinance sets.
new mexico.statute_name: New Mexico County and Municipal Zoning Enabling Act
new mexico.state_note: New Mexico has one unified enabling act for both counties and municipalities, and municipalities may also zone extraterritorially up to two miles beyond their boundaries. Variances are decided by the zoning authority itself on appeal, not always by a separate board of adjustment.

new york.variance_standard_note: Use variances and area variances use different tests. A use variance requires strict unnecessary hardship proved by a four-part test, including that no permitted use can yield a reasonable return. An area variance uses a looser practical-difficulty test, balancing the benefit to the applicant against detriment to the neighborhood.
new york.variance_process: Apply to the local Zoning Board of Appeals, usually after the enforcement officer denies a permit; the board holds a public hearing and must make written findings under the use-variance or area-variance standards. An appeal to the board from an enforcement officer's decision must generally be filed within 60 days.
new york.appeal_route: Appeal a Zoning Board of Appeals decision to the state Supreme Court (the trial-level court in New York) in a CPLR Article 78 proceeding, which reviews the record for legal error and whether the decision was arbitrary or supported by substantial evidence.
new york.nonconforming_note: State law does not address nonconforming uses, so each municipality sets its own rules. A lawful pre-existing use is generally protected as a vested property right, but it can be lost by abandonment, which requires intent to abandon plus actual discontinuance, or by discontinuance for the period set in the local ordinance, and it generally may not be enlarged or changed to a different nonconforming use.
new york.statute_name: Town Law Article 16; Village Law Article 7; General City Law Article 5-A (zoning enabling provisions)
new york.statute_cite: Town Law Section 267-b; Village Law Section 7-712-b; General City Law Section 81-b (Article 78 review: Town Law Section 267-c; Village Law Section 7-712-c; General City Law Section 81-c)
new york.agency_name: New York State Department of State, Office of Planning, Development and Community Infrastructure
new york.state_note: New York has three parallel zoning statutes, one each for towns, villages and cities, with nearly identical variance and 30-day Article 78 rules, plus a separate zoning system for New York City. LawHelpNY is the statewide free legal-help directory, not a direct-representation legal aid firm.

north carolina.variance_standard_note: A variance requires unnecessary hardship proved by all four statutory findings: hardship from strict application, peculiar conditions of the property, hardship not caused by the applicant, and consistency with the spirit and intent of the regulation. It is not enough to show the property could be more profitable without the variance.
north carolina.variance_process: Apply to the local board of adjustment, which holds a quasi-judicial public hearing, takes sworn evidence, and may grant a variance only if it finds all four statutory conditions based on competent, material and substantial evidence in the record.
north carolina.appeal_route: Appeal a board of adjustment decision to superior court by a petition for a writ of certiorari under N.C.G.S. Section 160D-1402; the court reviews the record rather than holding a new trial.
north carolina.nonconforming_note: Chapter 160D does not set a statewide abandonment period, so protection depends on the local ordinance. A lawful use that predates a zoning change may generally continue, but it usually may not be expanded, and it is lost if abandoned or discontinued for the period the local ordinance sets, commonly six to twenty-four months.
north carolina.statute_name: North Carolina Local Planning and Development Regulation (Chapter 160D)
north carolina.statute_cite: N.C.G.S. Chapter 160D (zoning: Sections 160D-701 to 160D-705; variance: Section 160D-705(d); judicial review: Sections 160D-1402 and 160D-1405)
north carolina.state_note: The 2019 recodification consolidated the old separate city and county planning and zoning statutes into a single Chapter 160D, effective January 1, 2021, so older citations to Chapters 153A and 160A are now outdated.

north dakota.variance_standard_note: The test differs between counties and cities and combines hardship and practical-difficulty language. The county statute allows adjustment where literal enforcement would result in great practical difficulties, unnecessary hardship or injustice; city boards of adjustment vary regulations in harmony with their general purpose and intent.
north dakota.variance_process: In a county, apply to the board of county commissioners, which itself decides variances and must state written findings; there is no separate county board of adjustment. In a city, apply to the board of adjustment, whose decision can then be appealed to the city governing body within 15 days.
north dakota.appeal_route: Appeal a county commission or city governing-body decision to district court under N.D.C.C. Section 28-34-01, which governs appeals from local governing bodies.
north dakota.nonconforming_note: A lawful use existing when a county zoning resolution is adopted may continue even though it does not conform. It is lost if discontinued for more than two years, after which any later use must conform, and the county may adopt reasonable regulations controlling nonconforming uses.
north dakota.statute_name: County Zoning Act and City Zoning Act
north dakota.statute_cite: N.D.C.C. Chapter 11-33 (counties, including Sections 11-33-11 to 11-33-14); Chapter 40-47 (cities, including Sections 40-47-07 to 40-47-11); appeal procedure: Section 28-34-01
north dakota.state_note: North Dakota is unusual in having no separate county board of adjustment: the county commissioners themselves decide county variances. Townships also have their own zoning powers, so a homeowner must first check whether the county, city or township controls the property.

ohio.variance_standard_note: The statute speaks of unnecessary hardship, but Ohio courts split the test. A use variance requires strict unnecessary hardship, while an area variance uses the looser practical-difficulty balancing test from Duncan v. Village of Middlefield, weighing factors such as the benefit to the owner, the character of the neighborhood and whether the difficulty can be avoided another way.
ohio.variance_process: Apply to the local board of zoning appeals (township, city or village), which holds a public hearing and may grant a variance only where literal enforcement would cause unnecessary hardship, the hardship comes from special conditions of the property, and the variance is the minimum necessary and not contrary to the public interest.
ohio.appeal_route: Appeal a board of zoning appeals decision to the Court of Common Pleas under Ohio Revised Code Chapter 2506 (and, for townships, Section 519.15); the court reviews whether the decision was unconstitutional, illegal, arbitrary, capricious or unreasonable, or unsupported by the preponderance of substantial, reliable and probative evidence.
ohio.nonconforming_note: A lawful use existing when zoning is enacted may continue even though it no longer conforms. Under the township and county statutes, protection is lost if the use is voluntarily discontinued for two years or more; municipalities may set a shorter discontinuance period in their own ordinances, and expansion is generally limited.
ohio.statute_name: Township Zoning Act (with separate municipal and county zoning chapters)
ohio.statute_cite: Ohio Rev. Code Chapter 519 (Sections 519.13 to 519.15, 519.19); see also Chapter 713 (municipalities) and Chapter 303 (counties); court appeal: Chapter 2506
ohio.state_note: Ohio has three separate zoning systems: townships under Chapter 519, municipalities under Chapter 713 with broad home-rule power, and counties under Chapter 303 for unincorporated areas, so the exact board and local rules depend on where the home sits. Ohio Legal Help is a statewide legal-information site, not a direct-representation legal aid firm.

oklahoma.variance_standard_note: A variance requires unnecessary hardship proved by four findings: the ordinance as applied to the particular property creates unnecessary hardship, the conditions are peculiar to that property, relief would not cause substantial detriment to the public good or impair the ordinance or comprehensive plan, and the variance is the minimum necessary to alleviate the hardship.
oklahoma.variance_process: Apply to the municipal board of adjustment, which holds a public hearing with mailed notice to nearby owners and may grant the variance in whole, in part or on reasonable conditions if it makes all four findings in writing.
oklahoma.appeal_route: Appeal a board of adjustment decision to the district court in the county where the municipality sits; under Section 44-110 the appeal is heard and tried de novo, meaning the court hears the case fresh rather than only reviewing the board's record.
oklahoma.nonconforming_note: A lawful nonconforming use as it existed when an ordinance was adopted may continue, but the municipality may provide for its termination by setting a period in which it must cease or by an amortization formula allowing a reasonable time to recover the investment. Nonconforming signs are protected unless altered to increase nonconformity or abandoned for more than two years.
oklahoma.statute_cite: 11 O.S. Sections 43-101 to 44-110 (variance: Section 44-107; nonconforming use: Section 44-107.1; appeal: Section 44-110)
oklahoma.state_note: Oklahoma's de novo district-court review of board of adjustment decisions is distinctive: the court retries the case instead of deferring to the board. The statute leaves the appeal filing deadline to be fixed by local ordinance, so the local ordinance must be checked, and counties have a separate 10-day appeal rule under 19 O.S. Section 19-866.24.

oregon.variance_standard_note: Oregon statutes do not set one statewide variance test. Each county or city zoning ordinance sets its own variance criteria, typically requiring special or unusual circumstances and unnecessary hardship or practical difficulty, and any variance must also be consistent with the local comprehensive plan and the statewide planning goals.
oregon.variance_process: Apply to the county or city planning department or hearings officer under the local ordinance, usually with a public hearing under ORS 215.416 for counties or ORS 227.175 for cities; the decision must be based on the standards in the local ordinance and comprehensive plan, with written findings.
oregon.appeal_route: After any required local appeal, appeal a final local land-use decision to the state Land Use Board of Appeals (LUBA) under ORS 197.830; LUBA reviews the record for legal error rather than holding a new hearing.
oregon.nonconforming_note: A lawful use existing when a zoning ordinance is enacted or amended may continue, and a change of ownership or occupancy is permitted. Alteration is limited to changes of no greater impact, restoration after fire or disaster must generally start within one year, and a use may not be resumed after a period of interruption or abandonment unless it then conforms.
oregon.statute_name: Oregon Land Use Planning Act; County Planning, Zoning and Housing Codes; City Planning and Zoning
oregon.statute_cite: ORS Chapter 197 (including Section 197.830, LUBA appeals); Chapter 215 (counties, including Sections 215.130 and 215.416); Chapter 227 (cities, including Sections 227.175 and 227.286)
oregon.agency_name: Oregon Department of Land Conservation and Development
oregon.state_note: Oregon runs a statewide land-use system: every local plan must comply with 19 statewide planning goals overseen by the Department of Land Conservation and Development, and LUBA is a specialized state board that hears land-use appeals. Local governments also may not deny a housing development inside an urban growth boundary that complies with clear and objective standards.

pennsylvania.variance_standard_note: Use variances and dimensional variances use the same five statutory factors but very different burdens. A use variance requires strict unnecessary hardship, including proof the property cannot be developed in conformity with the ordinance; a dimensional variance is judged more leniently, on practical difficulty and whether the relief is the minimum necessary.
pennsylvania.variance_process: Apply to the municipal Zoning Hearing Board, a quasi-judicial body; the board must hold a hearing within 60 days of receiving the application and issue a written decision within 45 days after the hearing closes, with findings on all five variance criteria in Section 910.2 of the Municipalities Planning Code.
pennsylvania.appeal_route: Appeal a Zoning Hearing Board decision to the Court of Common Pleas under Section 1002-A of the Municipalities Planning Code; the court generally reviews the board's record rather than taking new evidence.
pennsylvania.nonconforming_note: A use that was lawful before the ordinance changed may generally continue as a lawful nonconforming use and may be sold and continued by a new owner. It can be lost by abandonment, which generally requires both intent to abandon and actual discontinuance, and expansion or a change to a different nonconforming use is restricted by the local ordinance.
pennsylvania.statute_cite: 53 P.S. Sections 10101 et seq. (variance: Section 10910.2; zoning hearing board: Sections 10901 to 10909; appeal: Section 11002-A)
pennsylvania.agency_name: Pennsylvania Department of Community and Economic Development
pennsylvania.state_note: Pennsylvania's five-factor variance test is set by statute, but courts apply it much more strictly to use variances than to dimensional variances, so a homeowner seeking a different use faces a far harder case than one seeking a smaller setback. The 30-day appeal clock runs from the written decision and is not paused by further talks with the township.

rhode island.variance_standard_note: Use variances and dimensional variances use different tests. A use variance requires proof the land or structure cannot yield any beneficial use if forced to conform, a deliberately steep bar. A dimensional variance requires only that denial would cause more than a mere inconvenience and that the relief is the least necessary for reasonable enjoyment of the property.
rhode island.variance_process: File a variance application with the zoning officer for the local Zoning Board of Review, which holds a public hearing after at least 14 days' public notice and must enter evidence in the record showing the hardship comes from unique characteristics of the land or structure, was not caused by the applicant, and will not alter the general character of the area.
rhode island.appeal_route: Appeal a Zoning Board of Review decision to the Superior Court for the county where the city or town sits under R.I. Gen. Laws Section 45-24-69; the court reviews the record without a jury and does not substitute its judgment on questions of fact.
rhode island.nonconforming_note: A lawful use that predates a zoning change may generally continue as a nonconforming use. It is lost by abandonment or discontinuance for the period set in the local ordinance, and it generally may not be expanded or changed to a different nonconforming use without board approval.
rhode island.statute_cite: R.I. Gen. Laws Sections 45-24-27 to 45-24-72 (variance: Section 45-24-41; appeal: Section 45-24-69)
rhode island.agency_name: Rhode Island Division of Statewide Planning
rhode island.state_note: Rhode Island's 20-day appeal deadline is the shortest in this set and runs from when the decision is recorded and posted in the city or town clerk's office, so it can expire before a homeowner learns of a neighbor's approval. A 2024 statewide law also gives homeowners a right to build one accessory dwelling unit under set conditions.

south carolina.variance_standard_note: A variance requires unnecessary hardship proved by four written findings: extraordinary and exceptional conditions peculiar to the property, conditions that do not generally apply to other property nearby, application of the ordinance would effectively prohibit or unreasonably restrict use of the property, and the variance will not substantially harm adjacent property or the character of the district.
south carolina.variance_process: Apply to the local board of zoning appeals, which holds a public hearing and may grant a variance only if it makes and explains in writing all four findings in Section 6-29-800. The board may not use a variance to allow a use not otherwise permitted in the district, extend a nonconforming use, or change zoning district boundaries.
south carolina.appeal_route: Appeal a board of zoning appeals decision to the Circuit Court under Section 6-29-820 by filing a petition stating plainly how the decision is contrary to law; the property owner may also request pre-litigation mediation.
south carolina.nonconforming_note: State law lets the local governing body provide for the continuance, restoration, reconstruction, extension or substitution of nonconformities, but it also lets the locality terminate a nonconformity by setting a period in which it must cease or be brought into conformance, or by an amortization formula allowing recovery of the investment.
south carolina.statute_name: South Carolina Local Government Comprehensive Planning Enabling Act of 1994
south carolina.statute_cite: S.C. Code Ann. Sections 6-29-310 to 6-29-860 (zoning: Sections 6-29-710 to 6-29-850; nonconformities: Section 6-29-730; variance: Section 6-29-800; appeal: Section 6-29-820)
south carolina.state_note: South Carolina is distinctive in expressly barring use variances: a variance can never authorize a use the district does not already allow, so a homeowner who wants a different use must seek a rezoning or a special exception instead.

south dakota.variance_standard_note: A variance requires unnecessary hardship: because of special conditions on the property, literal enforcement of the ordinance would cause unnecessary hardship, and the variance must not harm the public interest. Financial loss alone is not enough.
south dakota.variance_process: Apply to the local board of adjustment (in many towns the city council or planning commission sits as the board). The board holds a public hearing and decides the request, and a two-thirds concurring vote is needed to grant a variance.
south dakota.appeal_route: An aggrieved person may petition a court of record (circuit court) for a writ of certiorari, asking the court to review whether the board's decision was illegal.
south dakota.nonconforming_note: A lawful use that existed when a zoning ordinance was adopted may continue even though it no longer conforms. If the nonconforming use is discontinued for more than one year, any later use must conform to the current ordinance.
south dakota.state_note: South Dakota has no single statewide zoning code; cities zone under SDCL chapter 11-4 and counties under chapter 11-2, so the local ordinance controls most details, including what counts as a nonconforming use.

tennessee.variance_standard_note: The statute blends both tests in one clause, speaking of peculiar and exceptional practical difficulties or undue hardship from the lot's shape, size, or topography. Local boards and courts also require a showing that strict enforcement would deprive the owner of any reasonable use of the land.
tennessee.variance_process: Apply to the local board of zoning appeals, which holds a public hearing after notice to nearby owners. You must show the hardship comes from conditions unique to your lot, not from something you did or from conditions shared by the whole neighborhood.
tennessee.appeal_route: A board of zoning appeals decision is reviewed by a petition for writ of certiorari in chancery or circuit court, which reviews the record rather than holding a new trial on the facts.
tennessee.nonconforming_note: A lawful use that predates a zoning change may generally continue, but local ordinances usually bar expanding it or changing it to a different nonconforming use, and discontinuing it can end the protection.
tennessee.legal_aid_name: Legal Aid Society of Middle Tennessee and the Cumberlands
tennessee.state_note: Tennessee counties zone under a separate part of the same chapter (Tenn. Code Ann. title 13, chapter 7, part 3), and the board must tell parties in writing of their right to seek judicial review under title 27, chapter 9.

texas.variance_standard_note: A variance requires unnecessary hardship: due to special conditions, literal enforcement would cause unnecessary hardship, the variance is not against the public interest, and the spirit of the ordinance is observed. Since 2021 the board may treat very high compliance costs or a large loss of buildable area as grounds for hardship.
texas.variance_process: Apply to the city's board of adjustment, which holds a public hearing and decides the request; a 75 percent concurring vote of the board is needed to grant a variance. The board cannot grant a variance that allows a land use the ordinance otherwise prohibits.
texas.appeal_route: An aggrieved person, a taxpayer, or a municipal officer may file a verified petition in district court, county court, or county court at law, and the court may issue a writ of certiorari to review the board's decision.
texas.nonconforming_note: Chapter 211 sets no single statewide rule for grandfathered uses, so protection depends on the city's ordinance; a lawful nonconforming use is commonly allowed to continue but not expand, and a city may phase some uses out over time. Separately, Chapter 245 protects vested rights in a pending permit application.
texas.state_note: Cities may zone only inside their city limits: a city cannot zone land in its extraterritorial jurisdiction (ETJ), where it may regulate subdivision and platting but not the use, height, bulk, or density of buildings. Texas counties have no general zoning power, and Houston has no comprehensive zoning ordinance.

utah.variance_standard_note: Utah uses an unreasonable-hardship test with five required findings, including special circumstances tied to the property and that the variance is essential to enjoy a substantial property right others in the zone have. A hardship that is self-imposed or purely economic does not count, and a use variance may not be granted at all.
utah.variance_process: Apply to the local appeal authority (a hearing officer, board, or other body the city or county designates), which decides the variance after a hearing. All five statutory findings must be made in the applicant's favor for the variance to be valid.
utah.appeal_route: After exhausting the local appeal-authority process, an adversely affected person may petition the district court for review; the court presumes the decision is valid and asks only whether it was arbitrary, capricious, or illegal.
utah.nonconforming_note: A nonconforming use or noncomplying structure may continue and pass to a future owner, and a structure destroyed by fire or other calamity may generally be rebuilt unless the use was abandoned. A city may end a use by amortization over a reasonable time to recover the investment, or for abandonment.
utah.statute_name: Municipal Land Use, Development, and Management Act
utah.agency_name: Utah League of Cities and Towns
utah.state_note: Utah also has a Property Rights Ombudsman in the Department of Commerce that gives free help on land-use disputes, and a landowner can ask it to arbitrate a takings claim, which pauses the 30-day court deadline.

vermont.variance_standard_note: Vermont has a strict five-part unnecessary-hardship test: unique physical conditions on the lot, no possibility of developing in strict conformity, hardship not created by the applicant, no harm to the neighborhood's character or neighbors, and the smallest variance possible.
vermont.variance_process: Apply to the local board of adjustment or development review board, which holds a hearing and must make written findings on all five hardship factors. A separate, easier test applies only to structures that are primarily renewable-energy structures.
vermont.appeal_route: An interested person who participated in the local proceeding may appeal to the Environmental Division of the Superior Court; Act 250 decisions of a District Environmental Commission are appealed the same way, also to the Environmental Division.
vermont.nonconforming_note: A lawful use that predates a zoning bylaw may continue, but local bylaws limit enlarging or changing it, and abandoning it can end the protection. A nonconforming use is separate from Act 250 approval, which a project may still need.
vermont.statute_name: Municipal and Regional Planning and Development Act
vermont.agency_name: Vermont League of Cities and Towns
vermont.legal_aid_name: Vermont Legal Aid (via VTLawHelp.org, with Legal Services Vermont)
vermont.state_note: Vermont is two-track: town zoning under 24 V.S.A. chapter 117 is only half the story, because Act 250 (10 V.S.A. chapter 151) requires a separate state land-use permit from a District Environmental Commission for larger developments, judged against ten criteria. Recent housing laws require towns to allow duplexes where single-family homes are allowed and have narrowed Act 250 review in town centers.

virginia.variance_standard_note: A variance is granted only if strict application would unreasonably restrict use of the property or if a physical condition of the property causes hardship, and the applicant must prove it by a preponderance of the evidence. The hardship must not be self-created, the variance cannot allow a prohibited use or change the zoning classification, and no other local process may offer the same relief.
virginia.variance_process: Apply to the local board of zoning appeals, which holds a public hearing and decides the request; the board's members are appointed by the circuit court. The applicant carries the burden of proof on every part of the variance test.
virginia.appeal_route: An aggrieved person may file a petition in the circuit court for the county or city, and the court reviews the board's decision by certiorari, with the board's findings of fact presumed correct unless rebutted by a preponderance of the evidence.
